investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only. The task-provided candidate domain (www.moucohotel.pt) was probed first via plain curl; it failed to resolve via DNS. Per instructions, a bounded WebSearch was then used purely as a DISCOVERY LEAD (never as evidence) to check whether a different official domain existed; it consistently returned the same moucohotel.pt domain plus a mouco.pt contact-email domain, both of which were then independently re-probed via direct curl (all three: www.moucohotel.pt, moucohotel.pt, mouco.pt) and via a third-party DNS-over-HTTPS resolver (dns.google), which confirmed genuine lame delegation / REFUSED at the domains' own authoritative nameservers, not a local/transient failure. Two independent third-party pages (an events aggregator and a listings magazine) were fetched via curl as discovery-lead evidence and both independently corroborate moucohotel.pt as the venue's real site. Because the live domain is unreachable, the Wayback Machine's public availability API and a retained historical snapshot (dated 2025-03-23, well before this investigation) were fetched via curl to check the last known live state; it showed the domain, when it did resolve, served a JS anti-bot/anti-headless challenge interstitial (Imunify360 WebShield) to plain requests rather than real content. A dependency-free, no-network Node offline-proof script mechanically re-confirmed every one of these findings from the retained fixture files. Level 1 was BLOCKED (both by current DNS unreachability and, historically, by an explicit anti-bot access-control challenge); escalation to Level 2/3/4 was not attempted because both blocking conditions are unaffected by deeper static/structural inspection or a browser session (DNS resolution is a prerequisite for all of them, and defeating the anti-headless fingerprinting is explicitly prohibited by policy).

probe_history.reason: Plain curl GETs (BandOnTheMap-SourceInvestigation/0.1 UA) against all three known/discovered domain forms of the candidate's official site (https://www.moucohotel.pt, https://moucohotel.pt, https://mouco.pt) all failed at the DNS resolution step (curl exit 6, 'Could not resolve host') — no HTTP request could even be sent. This was independently re-checked (not just trusted as a possible local resolver quirk) via a direct curl GET to a public third-party DNS-over-HTTPS API (dns.google): both mouco.pt and moucohotel.pt return DNS Status 2 (SERVFAIL) with an explicit 'Name servers refused query (lame delegation?)' comment, meaning the domains' own delegated authoritative nameservers (ns1/ns2.wtservers.com) actively refuse to answer — a genuine, source-side DNS misconfiguration/outage, not a fluke of this investigation's network. A general-network sanity check (fetching google.com and, separately, an unrelated .pt domain used in a prior investigation) both succeeded normally, ruling out a broader local DNS problem. Because the live site is unreachable, the last known live state was checked via the Wayback Machine's public availability API and one retained archived snapshot (2025-03-23, well over a year before this investigation) — that historical snapshot's own response headers ('x-archive-orig-server: imunify360-webshield/1.21') and body (title 'One moment, please...', text 'Please wait while your request is being verified...', plus an obfuscated script explicitly testing navigator.webdriver, headless/bytespider user-agent strings, plugin/mimetype array shape, and outerWidth/outerHeight for headless-browser fingerprints) show that even when the domain did resolve, a plain unauthenticated request was served an anti-bot/anti-headless JS challenge interstitial, not real site or event content. Two independent third-party pages (a Porto events aggregator and a Time Out Porto listing), retained as discovery-lead evidence only, both link to https://moucohotel.pt as the venue's official site, corroborating that this is genuinely the right candidate domain rather than a wrong guess. All of this was mechanically re-confirmed, with zero network access, by evidence/offline-proof.mjs. Escalation to Level 2 (STRUCTURAL) or Level 3 (BROWSER_OBSERVATION) was not attempted: DNS resolution is a hard prerequisite for both, and the historical evidence indicates the site is actively engineered to detect and block exactly the kind of automated/headless client that Level 3 would introduce — attempting to defeat that fingerprinting to get past it is explicitly prohibited by docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md, and escalating further would not change the current DNS outcome regardless.

Per instructions, a bounded WebSearch was used strictly as a DISCOVERY LEAD, and its leads were then independently re-checked with retained curl evidence: two separate third-party pages (agenda-porto.pt's own venue listing and Time Out Porto's listing, both retained in evidence/) independently and consistently link to https://moucohotel.pt as the venue's official site, and the Time Out page's own embedded schema.org PostalAddress JSON gives a Porto/Bonfim address (postalCode 4300-081) consistent with the task's stated location. A Wayback Machine snapshot (2025-03-23) of that exact domain also exists, corroborating the domain was genuinely live and hotel/venue-branded at some point (its response was gated behind a bot challenge, not a parked-domain or unrelated-business page). This is real, retained, cited evidence — but it is all THIRD-PARTY corroboration, never the source's own first-party self-description, and per docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md's 'Third-party sources' section a discovery lead must never be promoted to identity authority. identity.status is therefore PARTIAL (a real, evidenced, consistent candidate — not a wrong guess, not ambiguous/conflicting) rather than PROVEN, at LOW confidence, honestly reflecting that this investigation was never able to directly verify the source's own claim of itself.

blockers.description: The candidate's only known official domain(s) — www.moucohotel.pt, moucohotel.pt, and the associated mouco.pt — do not currently resolve via DNS. Confirmed by three direct curl attempts (all 'Could not resolve host', exit 6) and independently corroborated by a third-party DNS-over-HTTPS resolver reporting genuine lame delegation / REFUSED from the domains' own authoritative nameservers. No acquisition method (static, structural, or browser-based) can reach a host that does not resolve; this is not fixable by escalating the probe ladder.

Even the last known live state of the domain (Wayback Machine snapshot, 2025-03-23) shows it served every plain unauthenticated request an explicit anti-bot/anti-headless JS challenge interstitial (Imunify360 WebShield), including active fingerprinting for navigator.webdriver, headless/bytespider user agents, plugin/mimetype array shape, and zero outerWidth/outerHeight. Even if DNS is restored, plain static acquisition may continue to be challenge-gated by design, and a browser-based collector would need to defeat that fingerprinting — explicitly prohibited by docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md ('never defeat CAPTCHAs, bypass authentication... or evade explicit access controls').

reasons: The candidate's only known official domain(s) do not currently resolve via DNS — confirmed independently by direct curl (all three domain forms) and a third-party DNS-over-HTTPS resolver reporting genuine lame delegation at the domains' own authoritative nameservers, not a local network fluke (a control fetch of an unrelated, known-good .pt domain succeeded normally in the same session).

No first-party content of any kind — homepage, event list, or single event page — was ever retrieved from the candidate's own domain. All field_assessment entries are honestly UNKNOWN; none was fabricated to compensate.

The best available historical evidence (a pre-outage Wayback Machine snapshot) shows the site was, when it last resolved, gated behind an anti-bot/anti-headless JS challenge (Imunify360 WebShield) that explicitly fingerprints for automated clients — an explicit access-control boundary this policy prohibits attempting to defeat, so further escalation (Level 2/3/4) would not change the outcome and was correctly not attempted.

This is a legitimate, complete DEFER outcome per docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md's 'DEFER does not require exhausting the ladder' — escalating a browser/headless session merely to prove the investigation 'tried everything' before deferring is explicitly not required, and would face the identical DNS blocker regardless.

Re-investigation is recommended if/when the domain is observed to resolve again; in the meantime the venue remains a real, third-party-corroborated candidate (per identity.notes) that should not be discarded outright, only deferred.
